message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?" They want earliest reference from historical record. We can answer: earliest references are in the New Testament (Gospels), but also in non-Christian sources: Josephus (Antiquities 18.3), Tacitus (Annals 15.44), Pliny the Younger (letters 3.16), Suetonius (Lives of the Caesars 1.2). The earliest is probably Josephus, written around 93-94 AD. Also maybe the earliest mention is in the Gospel of Mark, written around 70-80 AD. But the question: "earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?" So we should mention earliest non-Christian references: Josephus, Tacitus, Pliny, Suetonius. Among them, Josephus is earliest, around 93-94 AD. Also the earliest Christian references are the Gospels, with Mark being earliest. So answer: earliest historical record is Josephus's Antiquities of the Jews, Book 18, Chapter 3, around 93-94 AD. Provide details. Also mention that some scholars debate authenticity of the passage.
